Heard learned Counsel for the petitioner and learned State Counsel for the respondents.

The present petition has been filed for the following main reliefs:-
"i. a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus commanding the opposite parties i.e. opposite party no. 4, not to make any interference or hindrance in peaceful functioning and carrying on the business of the petitioners of slaughtering and selling buffalow's meet in village Saddipur, P.S. Jahangirabad, District Barabanki.
ii. a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus commanding the opposite party no. 2 and 3 to take suitable action against the opposite party no. 4 with respect for complaint made by the petitioners through representation dated 7.12.2006 and 14.12.2006 contained in Annexure Nos. 1 and 2 to this writ petition."

In the present petition, on 12.02.2007, this Court has passed the following order:-
"Notice on behalf of opposite parties 1 to 4 has been accepted by the learned Chief Standing Counsel.
On behalf of opposite party no. 5, Sri Virendra Kumar Shukla has accepted notice.

In the meantime, it is provided that in case no bye-laws has been framed by the Zila Panchayat and there are no statutory rules or valid executive orders for restraining the petitioners from slaughtering and selling the buffalo meat at the particular place,
the petitioners' business shall not be interfered with."

Learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that in an identical matter, on 02.08.2019 the Division Bench of this Court in Writ Petition No. 7701 of 2008 (Hazi Hasan and two others Versus State of U.P. Thru Secy. Home and 4 Others) , has passed the order.

sentences.text:
The relevant portion of the order is quoted below:-
"1.

The petition seeks issuance of a writ in the nature of mandamus directing respondent No.4 (Station House Officer, P.S. Kotwali, district Barabanki) not to create hindrance in functioning and carrying business of the petitioners of slaughtering and selling buffaloes' meat in village Alapur, P.S. Kotwali, district Barabanki.

2. We have taken notice of the fact that when the case came up for hearing on 29.8.2008, the following order was passed :
"Notice on behalf of opposite parties 1 to 4 has been accepted by learned Chief Standing Counsel.
Notice on behalf of respondent no.5 has been accepted by Sri Virendra Kumar Shukla.

sentences.text:
In the meantime, it is provided that in case no bye laws has been framed by the Zila Panchayat and there are no statutory rules or valid executive orders for restraining the petitioners for slaughtering and selling the buffalo's meat at the particular place,
the petitioners' business shall not be interfered with. "

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners has pointed out that there has been a development in so much as the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 provides for making application for grant of licence for slaughtering the buffaloes and selling its meat.
Learned counsel contends that in the further development, the petitioners applied for licence on 25.4.2017.
However, neither licence has been granted nor the petitioners are being allowed to pursue their profession.
4. Learned counsel for the State Mr. Raj Baksh Singh, however, has pointed out that a new Act, viz Food Safety and Standards (Amendment) Act, 2017 has come into force.
The petitioners are required to make an application under the provisions of the Amendment Act of 2017.

The Court has been further assured that in case an application for grant of licence is filed under the Food Safety and Standards (Amendment) Act, 2017, decision thereon would be taken within a period of four weeks of making the application.
5. In view of the assurance given by learned counsel for the State Mr. Raj Baksh Singh, this petition is disposed of.
The petitioners would be at liberty to file an application under the Amendment Act of 2017(supra), which would be dealt with in accordance with law within four weeks."
Learned Counsel for the petitioner is requested that the similar benefit may be given to the present petitioner.
Learned Counsel for the respondent has no objection, to the prayer made by learned Counsel for the petitioner.

Accordingly, keeping in view the above said facts, the writ petition is disposed of with liberty to the petitioner to file a fresh application under the new Act, viz Food Safety and Standards (Amendment) Act, 2017,before the authority concerned within a period of two weeks from today.

If such application is preferred by the petitioner to the concerned authority, the same shall be considered and decided by him, strictly in accordance with law, expeditiously, say within a period of two weeks from the date of presentation of a certified copy of this order along with application.
With the aforesaid terms, the writ petition is disposed of finally. . .

(Saurabh Lavania,J.) (Anil Kumar,J.) Order Date :- 20.9.2019 Jyoti/-
